:::{#exr-fundamental-subspaces-practice}
#### Testing whether a linear system has a solution through the left null space

Part 2 of @thm-fundamental-subspaces says that $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})^\perp$,
so a [linear system](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-linear-system) $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ has a solution
exactly when $\vecf{b}$ is [orthogonal](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-orthogonal-vectors) to every vector of the [left null space](linear-algebra-rank-nullity.qmd#def-left-null-space).
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \sbmat{1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0},
\qquad
\vecf{b} = \sbmat{1 \\ 2 \\ 0}.
$$

Decide whether $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ has a solution, by testing $\vecf{b}$ against $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Find one nonzero vector of $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})$ whose third entry is $0$.

:::
